findings.description: F1 THE t119 TOPOLOGY AMENDMENT LEFT TWO UNPRICED CARRIERS OF THE SAME 'EXACTLY THREE PIPELINES' CLAIM - tests[5] (t0) AND tests[183] (t41, via backend/scripts/security_ops_verification.py:563). MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: leg 5 verbatim executes rc=1 on the current tree (this review ran it); the generator line asserts workflows == ["ci.yml", "deploy.yml", "e2e.yml"] while .github/workflows holds ci.yml, deploy.yml, e2e.yml, promote.yml, so leg 183's twice-executed regeneration yields WORKFLOW_SET_ROWS FAIL and the committed docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md is STALE-PASS (its line 71 reads 'WORKFLOW_SET_ROWS workflows=3 scan_jobs=0 PASS', generated pre-promote; the record footer is ALL_CHECKS_PASS 28 PASS, floor 18). These are the identical class t119's R2 record priced (131/143/155/162/167/177/191 + 227 via t111) - 'the workflow-listing legs extend their expected set to include promote.yml' - but the carrier sweep for that record evidently covered only legs carrying the literal three-workflow listing, not (a) the t0 find-exclusion guard, whose .github exclusion list encodes the claim as a NEGATIVE (anything not excluded is a violation) and (b) the security_ops generator, which encodes it as a sorted-equality. THIS FINDING PRICES THE DEBT; IT IS NOT A DEFECT IN t119's OWN FENCES (which were green and were verified on merged bytes) - it is a carrier-set incompleteness in the amendment record, exactly the failure mode WAL 1276's ruling 87b8ea05 already corrected once (agent_pack_verification.py:117 was the then-second carrier). FOLLOW-UP CARD PRICING IS IN checks.candidate_card_pricing; the recommendation is ONE card, not two (single-writer rule: both surfaces are the workflow-topology claim family, and the fix must be atomic or the tree ships one RED leg). REMEDY: definer grooms the follow-up card with the two leg amendments + the generator line + the report regeneration under the W2 eight-property index policy; builder edits generator + committed report; orchestrator applies the tests[5] and tests[183] index amendments in the card's merge window with forward AND reverse sha proofs.

F2 SECOND-ORDER CARRIER THIS REVIEW FOUND THAT NEITHER WAL 1276 NOR WAL 1287 NAMED: tests[161] (t36) IS ALSO RED TODAY, THROUGH ITS tests[5] NORMALISATION PREDICATE. Leg 161 executes rc=1 on the current tree (this review ran it and traced the failing line). Its internal normaliser strips the 13 phase-7 -path exclusions out of the live tests[5] command and then asserts the remainder contains the literal 'deploy.yml 2>/dev/null)', i.e. it re-derives the ORIGINAL t0 guard from the live entry; adding '! -name promote.yml' anywhere in tests[5] breaks that predicate no matter where the exclusion is inserted (this review tested both placements - after '! -name deploy.yml' and appended before '2>/dev/null)' - both leave the normalised string without the asserted literal). So the follow-up card's carrier set is THREE index legs, not two: 5, 183, 161. Leg 161's fix is a re-premise of the predicate to the post-amendment t0 guard (the same 'extend the expected set' rationale, no leg deletion, every other assertion of the leg preserved verbatim - including its simulated-tree negative controls, which is what makes leg 161 valuable and also what makes it fragile). CARRIED-DIGEST IMPACT IS ZERO: leg 161 asserts entry_sha equality only between its own temp copies, never against the live index, so amending tests[5] does not require touching leg 161's sha pins - only its predicate literal. REMEDY: include leg 161 in the follow-up card's amendment record with its own old/new command sha256 + entry_sha_before/after pair, and state explicitly in the record that the normalisation predicate is re-premised rather than relaxed (the ORIGINAL-guard fail-before control inside the leg must survive the amendment, otherwise the leg loses its discriminating power).

F3 THE tests[5] AMENDMENT IS NOT SAFE AS A NAIVE STRING APPEND - TWO HARD CONSTRAINTS THE GROOM MUST PIN. (a) docs/state/amend_index_entry6_phase7.cjs.ready is a byte-exact pre-state guard: it aborts with AMEND_ABORT unless tests[5].command equals the ORIGINAL t0 find text byte-for-byte. That script is already dead today (leg 161 normalises the live entry to reconstruct the pre-state precisely because the live command no longer matches), and any further edit to tests[5] buries it permanently. The follow-up card must NOT resurrect or re-point that .ready script; the amendment is a fresh record with its own sha protocol (t119's 1ecb995 window is the precedent: entry_sha_before assert, region replace, new_command_sha256 assert, entry_sha_after assert, reverse proven). (b) docs_verification.py's INDEX_ANCHORS (positions 16, 54, 131, 132, 133, 135, 215, 216) pins entry blobs by sha256; tests[5] is NOT an anchor, so the amendment itself needs no anchor rotation - but the same file's CARRIED_DIGESTS pins docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md at 4d69122b..., and regenerating that report for the four-workflow set MOVES that digest, so docs_verification.py's CARRIED_DIGESTS entry must be re-pinned by MEASUREMENT in the same commit as the regenerated report (t111/t116 CARRIED rotation precedent). MEASURED SAFETY: no stored leg executes docs_verification.py against a regenerated security_ops report - the only leg that runs docs_verification.py's own generator surface is leg 258, and it regenerates docs/criteria/docs_verification.md only - so the rotation window is safe if generator line + report + CARRIED_DIGESTS land in ONE commit. REMEDY: pin that atomicity as an AC ('the generator edit, the regenerated report and the CARRIED_DIGESTS re-pin are one commit; leg 258 green on the merged tree proves the window closed'). This is the same gap-absorbing discipline WAL 1276 recorded for the agent_pack carrier.

F4 THE RE-PREMISE CHOICE FOR THE WORKFLOW-TOPOLOGY CLAIM IS A REAL DESIGN DECISION AND THE TWO CANDIDATE SHAPES CONTRADICT EACH OTHER ACROSS CARDS - THE PLAN MUST PICK ONE NOW. Option ENUMERATE (what t119's R2 did): each carrier's expected set grows to {ci, e2e, deploy, promote}. It is lossless and cheap, but it is the third time this repo has extended a topology list by one name (t36's phase-7 amendment added 13 -path exclusions to leg 5; t119/R2 + ruling 87b8ea05 extended seven legs and two generator carriers), and every future workflow addition re-opens the same carrier sweep - the class is a standing RED generator, not a one-off. Option COUNT (this review's recommendation for the SECURITY/OPS family): re-premise the claim to what the requirement actually asserts - 'the pipeline set is exactly the four committed workflows, none auto-deploys to production, and the promote pipeline is human-gated' - i.e. assert a COUNT plus the load-bearing property (no automatic deploy trigger outside the gated workflow) instead of a name list. Option HYBRID (recommended, and the only shape that is honest about both): leg 5 keeps a name-list exclusion form (it is a general junk-file guard over security/ ops/ .github/, so its exclusions are inherently enumerative - converting it to a count would weaken it) but gains promote.yml in the exclusion list; the GENERATOR (security_ops_verification.py:563) is re-premised to the four-name set AND additionally asserts the human-gate property, because 'workflows == 3' was never the requirement's point - the point is which pipelines exist and which are automatic. Whichever is chosen, it must be chosen ONCE and applied to all three index carriers plus the generator in one card, or the records will disagree (leg 131 says four names, generator says four names, a future card says count=4 - three vocabularies for one fact). REMEDY: the groom states the chosen shape in the card's Constraints verbatim and the verifier's negative control proves the amended claim FIRES on a fifth unexpected workflow file (fail-before/pass-after both directions), so the re-premise cannot silently become a relaxation.

F5 ONE CARD, NOT TWO - SINGLE-WRITER RULE AND AN ATOMICITY REQUIREMENT BOTH POINT ONE WAY. The two (measured: three) unpriced surfaces share one owner family and one non-splittable window: surface A is the index pair tests[5] + tests[161] (orchestrator-owned index bytes, applied in the card's merge window under the W2 eight-property policy, definer authors the amendment record, builder writes ZERO index bytes); surface B is backend/scripts/security_ops_verification.py + docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md + the docs_verification.py CARRIED_DIGESTS re-pin (builder-owned product code and generator-owned report). Splitting them into two cards would ship an intermediate main where leg 183 is RED while leg 5 is green (or vice versa), violating the standing operator 'no new RED' directive that ruled WAL 1276 Option B down; and the two surfaces are the SAME claim, so a single card can carry one amendment record with three leg entries and one generator edit. GRANULARITY CHECK AGAINST limits.issue_granularity (max_acs 6, max_files 4, max_diff_lines 300, warn_only): the candidate card owns 3 product paths (generator, security_ops report, docs_verification.py) + 1 amendment-record artifact + the card/handoff JSONs = inside max_files; AC count lands at 5-6 (generator line + report regeneration + CARRIED re-pin + leg-5 amendment + leg-161 predicate + composite no-drift) = at the warn_only cap, not over; diff is a handful of lines in the generator, one report line, one constant, and one record - well inside 300. No split recommended. REMEDY: groom as one card; the composite AC re-attests the README triple pin, the index floor, and the t119/t116/t111 settlements so the card cannot silently undo the milestone it is cleaning up after.

F6 SWEEP-BASELINE ARITHMETIC RECONCILED, AND ONE STANDING-RED LEG IS MIS-CLASSIFIED BY THE MILESTONE'S OWN HANDOFFS - RECORD IT AS AN EXISTING RED, NOT A phase_20 NEW RED. WAL 1287's delta is arithmetically consistent: baseline 282/36, five healed (173, 227, 299, 300, 301) => 287/31, minus two new (5, 183) => 285/33, measured 283/35, leaving exactly two unexplained REDs. This review identified the likeliest candidate by measurement: tests[161] (t36) executes rc=1 TODAY (F2) and is therefore an existing RED that t119's merge created and no handoff priced - it belongs in the same follow-up card, and the corrected reconciliation is 285/33 minus leg 161 minus one leg this review cannot reproduce = 283/35. CAVEAT, STATED HONESTLY: this review did NOT re-run the full 318-leg sweep (82 minutes, and leg execution mutates committed reports on Windows-python - the class that contaminated legs 214/217 in the close-out and scratch/t116sim in the t116 window), so the last unit of the delta is UNMEASURED rather than explained; the orchestrator's next sweep should print the RED set and diff it against the phase_18 frozen-33 set to close the last unit. REMEDY: the follow-up card's close-out expectation is 'RED set = frozen set minus {5, 161, 183} minus the five recoveries, delta ZERO', and the sweep record must name the numbering base (0-based index; the t104 checker convention is 1-based as printed - WAL 1287's numbers are 0-based index positions, and mixing the two has already caused one transient misclassification in the t104-era record).

F7 README TRIPLE-PIN STATE VERIFIED BY INDEPENDENT RE-MEASUREMENT AT HEAD AND INTERNALLY CONSISTENT - NO ACTION, RECORDED SO THE NEXT CARD STARTS FROM MEASURED FACTS. Measured by this review on the working tree at main 9648df5: README.md is 421 cr-stripped lines with cr-stripped sha256 efded7fb4484f2cf... (raw CRLF file hashes differently at 48200b18..., which is why every pin is measured CR-stripped - the t110/t116 discipline), backend/scripts/docs_verification.py carries README_LINES = 421 and README_DIGEST = efded7fb4484f2cfabe2d1faee6e5d8c2b3a77162570a1613eba9374bcb789e4, and the README carries exactly 18 level-2 headings. The band is therefore 412 floor / 460 ceiling / 500 REQ-DOC-010 cap with 79 lines of headroom to the cap and 39 to the ceiling. The two legs that encode the band were re-read rather than trusted: leg 256 asserts the 340..460 band and the 18-H2 set (t116's written ceiling amendment), leg 258 asserts the 460 ceiling and the 'moved off the stale 29d22aff' report-dynamic rule. The leg-227 settlement landed as priced: its index entry is bad07ccc4a14 with the t116-measured report digest 7ace2eb5 and the 421/efded7fb README premises, and leg 227 was GREEN in the close-out sweep (one of the five recoveries) - the first GREEN on that leg since t59. REMEDY: none. Constraint for the NEXT README-moving card: any README edit must move the generator constants, the regenerated docs_verification.md and leg 227's premises in the same window, and leg 258's 'not byte-identical to the stale 29d22aff' assertion means the report must be regenerated, never hand-edited.

F8 THE README SCORING MAP'S TWELVE ROWS ARE INTERNALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE RECORDS AND THE HONEST GAPS ARE THE DISCLOSED ONES - CHECKED ROW-CLAIM-VS-RECORD, NOT ROW-CLAIM-VS-ADJECTIVE. This review read the shipped table (README.md lines 264-285) against docs/criteria/scoring_map/telemetry.md: the maxima are 2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,3(2/3),2,1(1/1),2(1/2) and every sub-maximal row carries its shortfall in the Claim line itself. The gaps are real and each is backed by a measured record line, not prose: CI/CD 2/3 - no environment separation (the human-gated promote pipeline exists and targets the SAME live service; WAL 1281's rehearsal run 39933068472 is the evidence the pipeline works, and the honest gap is that there is nothing non-production to promote THROUGH); Observability 1/2 - no shared trace ID, the OTel/Tempo/Loki block is commented YAML and the hosted /metrics returns the SPA fallback because render.yaml sets ENVIRONMENT to production (record line 24 states the probe); Alerting 1/1 at maximum with its classification disclosed (rules are real, the 2026-10-17 drill is measured, but the evaluator is the local compose stack - no Prometheus evaluates them continuously anywhere hosted); On-Call 1/2 - autonomy-policy.yaml defaults to deny, so the agent diagnoses and a human remediates by design. Note for the record: the dispatch's 'Alerting 1/2?' is not a discrepancy - the row is 1/1 at maximum and the telemetry record states why that is honest. REMEDY: none for the milestone. The one plan-level consequence is that the CI/CD gap is now the ONLY remaining scoring gap with a priced path (environment separation), and any future card that closes it must move README row 9, the delivery.md record and the scoring-map claim in one card - the same triple-pin discipline t116 established.

F9 STANDING BACKLOG ITEM CONFIRMED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT AND STAYS BACKLOG, NOT A phase_20 DEFECT: 193 OF 318 LEGS CARRY NO 'ac' KEY. This review enumerated the index: exactly 193 legs lack the key, all of them in the historical early-era range (0-based 0..192), every leg from 193 onward carrying it - the same figure and the same shape phase_19 W8 measured, unchanged across phase_20 (phase_20 added zero index legs; its index writes were amendments only). Neither t111/t116's settlements nor the candidate follow-up card is obliged to touch it, and the phase_18 disposition (explained to the operator, left in standing backlog) stands. REMEDY: keep it as its own amendment-class phase candidate, never smuggled into a product card - it is an index-wide metadata write with the full W2 eight-property cost per leg and no product benefit. Recorded here so the next coverage check reads '193 legs without ac metadata' as a known deferral.

F10 CRLF FIXTURE/REPORT HYGIENE IS NOW A THREE-EVENT CLASS IN phase_20's OWN WINDOW AND IS RECOMMENDED AS A SMALL CARD AT THE NEXT SURVEY (NOT CREATED HERE). The evidence in this milestone alone: (1) the close-out sweep's legs 214/217 went RED only because an untracked scratch/t116sim/ directory tripped leg 214's repo-wide relative-link walk, both re-ran GREEN after removal (WAL 1287); (2) the phase_19 record's 8-RED and 142/184 contaminations from Windows-python regeneration of committed reports during a builder/verifier window combined with an autocrlf flip; (3) the structural hazard this review confirmed while pricing F1 - leg 183's own command COPIES the committed report back on regeneration failure and writes into the working tree, so a leg that mutates a committed artifact is the norm, not the exception, and any sweep that runs it on a dirty tree mis-attributes. The bounded fix: the affected fixture/generator reads go through bytes or newline normalisation, sweep-runner preconditions assert core.autocrlf=true plus porcelain-clean before dispatching legs, and scratch directories are named into an excluded root (docs_verification.py's SKIP_DIRS already excludes 'scratch' at the repo root - leg 214's walk does not). This overlaps phase_19 W7/W10 and the existing t104 card (#110, 'codify the cmd.exe-vs-WSL environment rules in docs/commands.md'): CHECK t104's scope and EXTEND it rather than opening a duplicate. REMEDY: next survey opens or extends one hygiene card; the follow-up card in F1 must NOT absorb it.

F11 PROCESS VERDICT ON THE SEVEN-CARD CHAIN: EVERY DEVIATION WAS RULED IN-WINDOW BEFORE IT WAS RELIED ON, WHICH IS THE PLAN-LEVEL SUCCESS - AND THE ONE CLASS THAT SLIPPED IS THE CARRIER-SET SWEEP, WHICH IS NOW A PLAN-VOCABULARY CANDIDATE. Executed shape, read from the WAL and the shipped tree rather than from the WAL's adjectives: verification-record cluster t112/t113/t114/t115 closed first (d961491/8373176/db2c2b8/aab1ce0), t119 landed the gated promote pipeline with a real rehearsal (e9f8e1c + R2 window 1ecb995 + fence amendment 69f1206 + run 39933068472 SUCCESS with the human gate demonstrably exercised and operator-approved), t111 rewrote README Part 1 through a fence amendment rather than a pass-by-ruling where the leg WAS the discriminating-power proof (474fffd, ruling 2f7a91c4, ac_hash 6da2679a, merge 036ad9ad), t116 assembled Part 2 with the only unamended fences in the milestone and the ceiling amendment applied by the orchestrator in its merge window (51a9906 + 0e54bcc, forward/reverse sha proven, leg 227 settled with the priced README-pin overlay). Every one of those four deviations followed the same discipline: definer authors the record, orchestrator applies index bytes, verifier re-measures on merged bytes, negative controls prove the amendment is load-bearing. WHAT SLIPPED is narrow and nameable: when a card adds a file to a TOPOLOGY, the amendment record's carrier sweep must enumerate every surface that encodes the claim - including claims encoded as exclusions (leg 5), as generator equality (security_ops:563, agent_pack:117), and as reconstruction predicates inside other legs (leg 161) - not only legs that literally list the files. PLAN-VOCABULARY REMEDY (recommendation only, no card): the next survey adds a carrier-sweep checklist item to the amendment-record template - name-list legs, exclusion-list legs, generator constants, report literals, and cross-leg reconstruction predicates - so the class is priced before the merge instead of surfacing at close-out. That is the difference between t119's record (7 legs, 2 generators, complete for its own gates) and the tree it left behind (3 more carriers, caught only by the 82-minute sweep).

The CI/CD evidence chain is complete and each link is independently checkable: ci.yml on PR, e2e.yml, auto-CD on deploy, and the human-gated promote pipeline proven by rehearsal run 39933068472 (approver = the operator, both steps success, post-deploy health 200 with database postgresql / fallback_active false). The only coverage_gap FINDING is F1, and it is a CARRIER-SET gap in an amendment record, not a requirement gap.

checks.step_3_dependency: COMPLETE. The milestone's chain closed in the DAG's order: the verification-record cluster (t112-t115) before the README parts that cite them, t119 before t111 (the ordering correction at WAL 1277 stopped a mis-dispatched t111 builder at 17s with zero damage rather than letting t111 re-pin against a pre-promote tree), t111 before t116 (t116's re-pin needed t111's shipped digests), and t116's ceiling amendment applied inside t116's own merge window rather than early. No cycle, no orphan, no card merged with an unclosed dependency. The follow-up card recommended in F1/F5 has NO dependency on any phase_20 card (they are closed) and blocks nothing except the sweep-baseline expectation in F6.
checks.step_4_duplicate_contradiction: COMPLETE with one real finding. No duplicate ACs across the seven cards - the records partition the twelve dimensions by cluster and the README table's claims are string-equal to the records by t116's own fence (verified: the twelve rows' maxima and the record claims agree, F8). The one genuine contradiction risk is F4: the repo now encodes the workflow-topology fact in at least four vocabularies (leg 131's name-list exclusion, leg 5's find exclusion, security_ops_verification.py's sorted equality, agent_pack_verification.py's EXPECTED_WORKFLOWS tuple) and a re-premise that changes one family's shape without changing the others leaves one fact with three vocabularies - F4 requires a single chosen shape applied across all carriers in one card. Also checked and clean: leg 227's settlement record, the leg 256/258 ceiling amendment, and leg 258's dynamic report-count rule do not contradict each other (227 pins the README premises, 256/258 bound the band, 258 refuses a stale report digest - three different assertions about three different objects).
checks.candidate_card_pricing: ONE CARD (F5), tentatively 'workflow-topology carrier completion (promote.yml)'. SURFACES AND OWNERS: (1) backend/scripts/security_ops_verification.py:563 - builder; the WORKFLOW_SET_ROWS assertion re-premised per F4, plus the human-gate property if the hybrid shape is chosen; ruff/mypy clean is already inside leg 183's own gate. (2) docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md - builder; regenerated by the generator, never hand-edited; expected delta is EXACTLY the WORKFLOW_SET_ROWS line (workflows=3 -> workflows=4) with ALL_CHECKS_PASS 28 PASS and the 29-row CARRIED count unchanged; determinism is proven by leg 183's own two-run byte-stability (the leg regenerates twice and cmp -s's both runs), so the report must be byte-stable across the amend. (3) backend/scripts/docs_verification.py CARRIED_DIGESTS['docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md'] 4d69122b... -> the regenerated measured digest - builder, SAME commit as (1)+(2) (F3). (4) docs/state/merge_test_index.json tests[5] - ORCHESTRATOR in the card's merge window; add the promote.yml exclusion to the .github name list, every other byte of the command preserved; measured: the amended command executes rc=0 (this review ran it). (5) tests[161] - orchestrator; re-premise the normalisation predicate to the post-amendment t0 guard (F2); measured: leg 161 is RED today and its failure line is the normalised-pre-state assert. (6) tests[183] - orchestrator only if its command text changes; if the fix is confined to the generator + report, leg 183 heals without an index write - THE GROOM MUST STATE WHICH, because the amendment record must match what actually changes. PROTOCOL per amendment: entry_sha_before assert, single region replace, new_command_sha256 assert, entry_sha_after assert, reverse applied and proven (t119's 1ecb995 window is the byte-proven precedent; WAL 1285's leg 227 overlay is the second). NO leg deleted; no verifier threshold touched; builder writes ZERO index bytes; definer authors the record. RISK ANALYSIS: (a) leg 183 regenerates the report TWICE per run and twice per sweep - if the generator's output were ever non-deterministic the leg would flake rather than fail cleanly; mitigated by the leg's own cmp -s and by this review's finding that the report is fully file-derived (no datetime/date usage in the generator; repo_root is parameterised, so a temp-clone rehearsal is safe). (b) leg 5's exclusion list is a growth pattern - every future workflow, security/ or ops/ file re-opens this card class; F4's enumerate-vs-count decision is the mitigation and leg 5's junk-guard nature argues for keeping enumeration there while moving the SEMANTIC claim into the generator. (c) the amend_index_entry6_phase7.cjs.ready byte-guard is already dead and stays dead (F3a) - do not re-point it. (d) docs_verification.py's INDEX_ANCHORS do not include position 5, so no anchor rotation is needed - but the same file's CARRIED_DIGESTS must rotate in the same commit (F3b). (e) sweep attribution: the fix must land with a named close-out expectation (F6) or the next close-out will again find unexplained RED units. NOT-CARD ITEMS: the 193/318 ac-key gap (F9) and CRLF/scratch hygiene (F10) stay backlog; environment separation (the CI/CD 2/3 gap) is a separate operator-scoped decision, not this card.
